recentItems.title: Donald Trump launches Trump TV
recentItems.description:
President Donald Trump has launched his own TV channel, Trump TV, giving him a platform to communicate directly with viewers and present his own coverage and message.

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

The launch comes as tensions between Trump and the US media escalate, with several major outlets blocked from White House coverage and now suing the administration.

With his own platform, Trump can deliver his message directly, without the traditional media middleman. The question is: will Americans tune in?

recentItems.title: White House launches Trump TV as row with major networks intensifies
recentItems.description:
The White House is taking the bully pulpit to new levels - launching its own YouTube channel to broadcast what it described as "Trump's greatest hits", 24 hours a day.

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

It follows a decision by all the major US broadcasters to suspend their pool coverage of Trump  in protest at his decision to ban CNN, MSNow and Politico from the White House.  

Those three outlets are now taking legal action over the move.

recentItems.title: ‘LOW ENERGY DONALD’ - Was Trump’s UN speech less fiery than usual?
recentItems.description:
On this episode of TrumpWorld, Matt Frei and Anushka Asthana discuss Donald Trump’s speech to the UN General Assembly.

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

During his 37 minute speech there were familiar rants against the media, Cuba and Iran, who he threatened with “annihilation”.

This time though, not only did he stay mainly on script - but he also seemed ‘lower energy’ than usual, according to Matt Frei.

recentItems.title: Tackling NEETs crisis: New scheme launched to help kids in care
recentItems.description:
The government borrowed another £18 billion last month, up a fifth on a year ago.

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

It reveals the pressure on Chancellor John Healey to boost economic growth in next month's budget. Cutting the rise in young people who are not in employment, education or training would help. 

One charity is helping young people in the care system into a better future, by funding places for them in private schools. It's backed by personal funding from the entrepreneur John Roberts, who told this programme that any politician who didn't support the scheme had "blood on their hands”.

recentItems.title: Trump Meets Burnham at UN
recentItems.description:
Before his meeting with Andy Burnham at the United Nations in New York, President Trump used his speech to the General Assembly to again threaten Iran with annihilation. 

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

Though he also predicted a deal to resolve the conflict would happen after the mid-term elections in November. 

Trump seemed to get along well with Andy Burnham - describing him as a "natural business person" and adding "he gets it". Later this week President Trump will meet China’s President Xi Jinping.

recentItems.title: UK Government emergency plan: should we be stockpiling?
recentItems.description:
Why is everyone talking about stockpiling?

The UK government has confirmed to Channel 4 News that it is now set to launch a new plan to prepare ready for emergencies.

Extreme weather, cyber attacks and AI interference are just some of the dangers the government has said we should get ready for.
But, as the wait goes on for official guidance to be published. Some content creators have filled that void.

In this episode of the breakdown we look at why the government is talking about being prepared now, what being prepared actually looks like, and how worried we should actually be.
We also speak to Professor Hannah Cloke, an expert on risk and resilience from the University of Reading.

The government told the breakdown in a statement that it will launch a public awareness campaign - and that these were “normal practice across Europe”.
A spokesperson added: Following a difficult summer, the Prime Minister has been clear that Britain must become more resilient and better prepared for the challenges we face.”
